steps.what: Provide individualized instruction and adapt explanations to the learner's responses

tasks.design: Keep individualized instruction and practical feedback with the teacher. Existing resources in {LMS} support the session; no automated tutor is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The useful explanation depends on the learner's actual response and practical technique.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing learning materials already support teacher-led instruction.
tasks.still_hard: A learner can repeat an answer without understanding or performing the skill safely.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise the misconception and adjust the demonstration at the right moment.
tasks.altitude: Direct teaching time and teaching decisions remain unchanged.

reach.task: Adapt support to persistent learning barriers

evidence.claim: Responsive practical instruction remains human work; the digest's feedback tools do not establish replacement of vocational tutoring.

assumptions: Boundary is the live individual teaching session; needs determination, curriculum preparation and record maintenance are assigned to their own tasks.
No new structured input, model assessment or software deployment is introduced.
Existing native learning resources remain sufficient; no incremental upkeep is created, so zero new work is justified.
unknowns: Learner support needs and practical safety requirements
research_questions: Which misconceptions require an observed demonstration rather than another written explanation?

already_counted.description: Individual instruction and responsive practical feedback

incremental.description: No new workflow or system maintenance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. Direct instruction is retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain student records and prepare reports

steps.what: Capture grades, attendance and completed training activities
Copy records into required registers and prepare standard reports
Resolve record discrepancies and confirm reports for authorised recipients

tasks.design: Capture records once in {LMS}, then configure native exports or a fixed mapping into the required register and report. Keep discrepancy resolution and final report confirmation with the teacher; the integration does not award grades.
tasks.previous_blocker: A required register and learning system can demand duplicate entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record exports and fixed report mappings can remove that transcription.
tasks.still_hard: Attendance and completion require trustworthy observations; mismatched student identifiers require resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Notice inconsistent records and distinguish a clerical problem from a learning concern.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate recording; grade authority stays unchanged.

reach.learn: Student identifiers, reporting dates and correction history

evidence.claim: Radboud guidance requires grades held in Brightspace to also be published in OSIRIS, illustrating a separate-register workflow without establishing this school's setup.
The proposed fixed mappings and time reduction are model knowledge, conditional on actual duplicate recording.

assumptions: Boundary includes this teacher's capture, transcription and reporting; assessment decisions that produce authorised grades occur in the assessment task and are unchanged.

The vocational teacher produces student ID, activity ID, attendance date and status, completion date, authorised grade and grading version in s1. All 40 capture hours remain, including checking imported grades against the examiner's authorised result.

s2 reads those fields and the education administrator's existing report specification. Missing IDs or incompatible grade versions stop mapping and return to s3 manual reconciliation; no inference fills an absent grade.
Test native register exports and report configuration before custom code. Existing scheduled exports earn no labour saving.
research_questions: Can a parallel reporting cycle remove thirty transcription hours without increasing capture or correction time?

already_counted.description: Source capture, discrepancy correction and final report confirmation

incremental.description: Check failed mappings and report changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact report version, student rows, reporting period and resolved discrepancies; corrections void confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70; gross 30%, minus four focal upkeep gives 26% central net. Low assumes ten removable duplicate-entry hours with unchanged capture, review and upkeep. An already integrated school has no such gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Select curriculum outcomes, occupational requirements and teaching constraints
Develop curricula, lesson sequences and instructional activities

loop.purpose: Draft a lesson sequence and activities aligned with the teacher's brief
loop.input: Curriculum brief and approved teaching resources
loop.output: Draft sequence with outcome and source links
loop.check: Teacher checks each activity teaches the linked skill, prerequisites are met and practical hazards are addressed
loop.stop: One revision, then manual planning if alignment or safety remains uncertain
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates set structure but cannot choose explanations and activities for varied vocational skills

steps.what: Review practical feasibility and approve the instructional plan

tasks.design: Use a template in {DOCS} and a bounded drafting loop to turn the teacher's curriculum brief into proposed sequences and activities. The teacher checks educational meaning, practical feasibility and safety before approving a plan for use in {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rewriting similar lesson structures takes time while each occupational skill needs tailored activities.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can reuse approved resources without deciding qualification requirements.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible activity may miss the actual practical skill or assume unavailable equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Choose worthwhile learning experiences and judge safe practical progression.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft writing; curriculum responsibility stays with the teacher.

reach.task: Align practical courses across the programme
reach.learn: Outcome mapping, equipment dependencies and progression

evidence.claim: A bounded curriculum draft with teacher alignment and safety review is an E1 design, not a measured case from the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is curriculum planning, excluding live instruction, learner needs determination and assessment decisions.

The teacher captures outcome identifiers, skill descriptions, learner prerequisites, duration and equipment limits in s1; all 30 hours remain. Source resources and their versions are selected there, and absent constraints require manual clarification rather than model invention.

Test native lesson templates and reuse first; add the bounded loop only for semantic activity drafting. Retained s2 time covers draft review and one revision; s3 independently checks the final practical plan.
research_questions: Do draft activities genuinely teach each selected skill without adding safety or feasibility corrections?

already_counted.description: Brief preparation, draft correction and final plan approval

incremental.description: Maintain approved resources and review recurring draft errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact curriculum version with outcomes, activities, durations, safety requirements and equipment assumptions; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+20+30=80; gross 20%, minus four upkeep gives 16% central net. Low assumes only seven writing hours removed because practical activities need extensive revision.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine student and worker training needs

steps.what: Observe performance and discuss training needs with students or workers
Determine training priorities from evidence and learner circumstances

tasks.design: Keep observation, discussion and training-priority decisions with the teacher. Existing records in {LMS} inform the conversation; no automated learner ranking is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Written records alone do not show why a practical skill is missing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing competency descriptions and work samples support human diagnosis.
tasks.still_hard: A learner's confidence, access to practice and actual competence can differ.
tasks.human_edge: Identify the cause of a gap and agree achievable next steps.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains the same diagnostic responsibility and time.

reach.learn: Workplace standards and available practice tasks

evidence.claim: Practical needs determination remains human observation and judgement; no saving is assumed from student records alone.

assumptions: Boundary covers needs determination, excluding subsequent teaching, curriculum planning and formal grade decisions.
No automated decision uses a new structured learner profile; existing evidence is considered directly by the teacher.
No system change is proposed. Existing native record views suffice and incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Required workplace competencies and available evidence
research_questions: Which training gaps need direct observation before a priority can be agreed?

already_counted.description: Performance observation, conversation and priority decision

incremental.description: No new process or system upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, zero gross saving and zero incremental upkeep. The design retains observation and training decisions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less duplicate student reporting and curriculum drafting, with practical instruction and training decisions retained.
reach: Coordinate practical progression with the instructional coordinator
role.ambitious_version: A vocational teacher with more attention available for learners' actual practical difficulties.
